segments.text: At the Dunphy house, Luke has a huge school project on Vincent van Gogh due the next day, and he hasn’t started. Haley also suddenly announces that she needs forty cupcakes for a fundraiser. Claire takes the cupcakes and tells Phil to stay on top of Luke.

segments.text: Phil refuses to micromanage him. He says Luke just needs the right tools and a little space. The problem is that Phil is even easier to distract than Luke.

segments.text: Every few minutes he wanders away to fix something around the house, and Claire becomes more and more convinced that the project is going to be a disaster.

segments.text: Claire handles Haley in the exact opposite way. She shows her how to make the cupcakes, then keeps stepping in every time Haley does something wrong until Claire is basically doing the whole job herself.

segments.text: Later, Claire checks Luke’s room expecting nothing. Instead, she finds a creative display that he mostly built on his own. Luke split it into van Gogh’s life on one side and his paintings on the other, and it actually works.

segments.text: Manny takes that advice seriously. After Mitchell gets sprayed by a skunk, Jay and Manny keep teasing him until Mitchell finally gets angry. That’s when Jay tells him what’s really going on.

segments.text: Manny wasn’t invited to a party because some kids he thought were his friends think he’s weird. Jay doesn’t know how to talk to him about it, so he brought Mitchell along because he thought Mitchell might.

segments.text: Mitchell later tells Manny that kids called him weird too. He says the strange thing about growing up is that everybody spends years terrified of being different, and then suddenly being different becomes something people want.

segments.text: While the boys are out, Cameron takes Gloria to dinner because he wants them to be closer friends. He tries so hard to impress her that he orders an insanely spicy dish even after she warns him not to. He can barely eat it.
